newsitem.title: LATVIA: LATVIA-NEW GOVERNMENT IN BUDGET, PRIVATISATION PLEDGES.
newsitem.headline: LATVIA-NEW GOVERNMENT IN BUDGET, PRIVATISATION PLEDGES.

text.p: Prime Minister-candidate Guntar Krasts on Wednesday signed the new government's declaration with the heads of the leading parties, making pledges on the fiscal deficit and completing privatisation.
The new government declaration is similar to the previous one of outgoing prime minister, Andris Shkele.

"Strengthening of democracy, of the security of the state and citizens, economic prosperity and the growth of national well-being, inclusion in the European Union and stable, national development -- these are the aims that this government has set itself," the declaration said.
It said the government would aim at a fiscal deficit of 0.9 percent of GDP this and 0.5 percent next year.
However, it said that the deficit may be allowed to rise to one percent of GDP for the state investment programme.
It did not give a specific figure for the budget deficit, expected to be between 10 and 12 million lats.
The declaration also had an inflation target of nine percent for 1997 and seven percent for next year. Inflation in June was 7.5 percent year-on-year.
The declaration also pledges to speed privatisation and complete it by July 1 of next year and to issue medium-term state Treasury bills next year.
It also aims to restructure Latvian Railways along market economy lines and increase the minimum wage by 10 percent in 1998.
